toegepas.voor: Die water maak die droë dele nat en dik.
toegepas.na: Die water maak van die droë dele 'n nat, dik mengsel.
toegepas.rede_vinder: Dry parts cannot themselves become 'dik'; it is the mixture that turns wet and thick, so the sentence reads more clearly this way without changing what it says.
toegepas.fout: The sentence says the dry parts themselves become 'dik', which sand and gravel do not; it is the mixture that turns wet and thick.
toegepas.rede_keurder: The proposal says what happens precisely (water turns the dry parts into a wet, thick mixture) without adding a fact or touching a protected wording.

toegepas.voor: verhard daar tot een harde stuk
toegepas.na: verhard daar tot een vaste stuk
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'verhard ... tot een harde stuk' repeats itself; 'vaste stuk' avoids the repetition and matches the wording of the sement definition.
toegepas.fout: 'verhard daar tot een harde stuk' is a tautology: the verb already says it becomes hard.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'vaste stuk' removes the repetition, keeps the meaning (hardness is still carried by 'verhard'), and echoes the shared sement definition's 'een vaste stuk'.

toegepas.na: plak stukke papier aan mekaar vas
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'aan mekaar' needs more than one thing to refer to; 'papier' alone is a mass noun.
toegepas.fout: 'mekaar' needs a plural antecedent, but 'papier' is a mass noun here.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'stukke papier' gives 'aan mekaar' something to refer to, a small grammatical fix that adds no information.

laat_vaar.voor: meng 'n bakker meel en water en nog 'n paar goed saam
laat_vaar.na: meng 'n bakker meel, water en 'n paar ander dinge saam
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: This removes the double 'en ... en', and swaps the spoken-style 'goed' for 'dinge', which suits written study text better.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'meel en water en nog 'n paar goed' is natural, plain spoken Afrikaans that a Grade 5 reader follows easily; the proposal is a lateral move toward a more formal register.

vlae.teks: Wanneer 'n nat of sagte mengsel na 'n ruk hard word.
vlae.rede: The headword is a verb, but the definition is a 'wanneer' clause, so it describes a situation instead of the action. That is common in school glossaries, so it is not changed here. A reviewer or writer may prefer an 'Om ... te' form.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: wat jy kan uitgooi soos meel
laat_vaar_vorige.na: wat jy soos meel kan uitgooi
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: The comparison sits more naturally before the verb cluster in an Afrikaans subordinate clause.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: A 'soos' comparison placed after the verb cluster is normal Afrikaans; the reorder is lateral.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: strooi die poeier stadig daarby in
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'daarby in' is an awkward combination; 'daarin' says plainly that the powder goes into the water.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'daarby in' is ordinary recipe Afrikaans and carries the sense of adding to the water; 'daarin' drops that and is no clearer.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: Two coordinate adjectives that each describe the noun are separated by a comma.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: Afrikaans commonly writes stacked adjectives without a comma, and the lesson already writes 'droë wit poeier' without one; the comma is lateral and inconsistent.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: In written standard Afrikaans an object such as a brick is referred to with 'dit', not the colloquial 'hy'.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'hy' for a concrete object such as a brick is standard Afrikaans, the lesson uses 'sy' for the jelly elsewhere, and 'dit' in the sentence before already refers to the clay.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Wat verander en wat bly dieselfde
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: The accent on 'ná' marks the time meaning 'after', set against 'voor', as AWS allows for clarity.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: Set against 'voor', the temporal 'na' is already clear, so AWS does not call for the accent, and the lesson writes 'na' without one elsewhere.
